metadata.audience: High school students + parents planning service hours
metadata.purpose: Insider volunteer insights — what AOs actually look for, hidden leadership pathways, scholarship-linked service, in-state vs national org access, the 'sustained vs sporadic' nuance.

sections.title: What admissions officers actually look for in service

items.label: Sustained > sporadic, by a lot
items.detail: AOs at HYPSM-tier schools have repeatedly published that 200 hours at one organization beats 200 hours across 5 organizations. Demonstrates commitment, growth, and depth of impact. Pick one or two and stay 3-4 years.

items.label: Leadership growth beats hour count
items.detail: Moving from volunteer → committee member → coordinator → board liaison over 4 years tells a story. 500 hours of unchanged volunteer role tells a different story. Story matters more than count.

items.label: Don't pad the activity list
items.detail: Common App allows 10 activities. AOs see padded lists and discount the depth of every entry. Better to list 5 substantive activities than 10 light ones.

items.label: CIT pipeline at major camps
items.detail: YMCA, Camp Fire, BGCA all have Counselor-In-Training programs for ages 13-15. Free or discounted attendance + leadership training. Apply year before turning 14. Often leads to paid junior counselor role at 16-17 — a strong work + leadership signal.

items.label: Hospital 'Junior Volunteer Leadership Council'
items.detail: Most major hospitals' Junior Volunteer programs have an internal leadership track — student board, peer mentor program, etc. Self-nominate after 6 months as regular volunteer. Way fewer applicants than the regular junior volunteer pool.

items.label: Local nonprofit board student seat
items.detail: Many small-to-mid nonprofits have a 'student member' seat on their board, often unfilled. Email the executive director directly with a brief proposal. Boards under 15 members often welcome the youth perspective.

items.label: Bonner Scholars Program
items.detail: 60+ colleges offer the Bonner Scholarship — full or partial tuition in exchange for service commitment during college. Apply during senior-year college applications. Demonstrates pre-college service commitment is the eligibility differentiator.

items.label: Coca-Cola Scholars Foundation
items.detail: 150 students/year, $20K each. Service is one of three pillars (leadership + academics + service). Application opens August of senior year. Sustained multi-year service is the differentiator vs episodic.

items.label: AmeriCorps Education Award
items.detail: Year-long full-time service after HS = ~$7K toward college. Stack with Pell Grant + state aid. City Year (year-long teaching support) is the highest-prestige program in the network.

sections.title: What NOT to do (voluntourism + checkbox traps)

items.label: International 'mission trip' service is heavily discounted by AOs
items.detail: Two weeks building a school in another country reads as expensive tourism. AOs explicitly devalue these unless the family has a sustained connection to the community. If you must do international service, do it through year-round partnership orgs that serve via virtual mentorship + occasional in-person visits, not 1-2 week trips.

items.label: 'Service hour' graduation requirements don't impress
items.detail: Most HS districts require 40-100 service hours to graduate. Meeting this minimum is invisible. Doubling it without a clear story is also invisible. Triple it AND have growth + impact and now you have something.

items.label: Avoid 'starting your own nonprofit' unless you really mean it
items.detail: AOs have seen 50,000 student-founded nonprofits. The ones that move the needle have real 501(c)(3) status, sustained 3+ year operating history, audited finances, and measurable impact. Most student nonprofits don't meet this bar — and AOs can tell from the application.

sections.title: From the field — fresh insider notes (auto-discovered)

items.label: Washington Trails Association — 48-hour signup cliff is hard, but email opens a back door
items.detail: WTA work parties are auto-removed from the public schedule 48 hours before start time, even if half-empty — there's no on-page "sign up anyway" button. Inside that window, email volunteer@wta.org directly: crew leaders can sometimes squeeze one more if tools and lunch counts permit. Outside the email path, you're locked out. Plan teen weekend trail days the Wednesday before, not the Friday of. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Washington Trails Association Volunteer Trail Work Parties

items.label: WTA — Free trailhead day pass + free annual Discover Pass at 5+ days/yr
items.detail: WTA hands every work-party volunteer a free Discover-Pass-equivalent day pass at the trailhead — that alone covers the $11.50 day-use parking fee and offsets gas. Volunteer 5+ days in a calendar year and you earn a free annual Discover Pass ($30 value). For a teen building service hours over a summer, that's roughly $50-$70 in family parking costs back in your pocket — never marketed up-front. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Washington Trails Association Volunteer Trail Work Parties

items.label: WTA — Dress code is enforced, not requested. Sneakers = sent home.
items.detail: Long pants and sturdy CLOSED-TOE shoes are mandatory at the trailhead — crew leaders WILL turn volunteers away in shorts, leggings, or athletic sneakers without sturdy soles. The slot you signed up for is just lost. For sawyer crews (the prestige track for repeat teen volunteers), fully LEATHER boots are required, not just any closed-toe — plus long loose-fit pants (not athletic tights) and side-shielded eye protection. Plan a $60-$80 boot purchase if a teen wants to advance to saw work. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Washington Trails Association Volunteer Trail Work Parties

items.label: Hopelink — 1-week background check is on the critical path; can't volunteer same week
items.detail: Every Hopelink volunteer 16+ must pass a Washington State Patrol background check BEFORE attending the required virtual New Volunteer Orientation. Processing takes up to a week, then orientation is invite-only on a fixed schedule. Net: you cannot decide on a Sunday to volunteer next Saturday. Apply 2-3 weeks before any service-hours deadline. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Hopelink Volunteer (Eastside / North & East King County)

items.label: Hopelink — Most shifts are M-Th business hours; only a handful work for high-schoolers in school
items.detail: Stated openly on the page: "Most of our volunteer opportunities occur Monday through Thursday during regular business hours." The teen-feasible exceptions are narrow — Wednesday evening Avondale Park dinners (group prep + serve a meal for ~50 residents), and Friday afternoon Kirkland Warehouse sorting. Otherwise, school-break weeks are when teens can sustain weekly hours. Plan summer + winter break service-hour blocks accordingly. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Hopelink Volunteer (Eastside / North & East King County)

items.label: Hopelink — Holiday-season group slots fill 4 MONTHS out; lock Q4 by July
items.detail: Hopelink books group volunteer slots up to 16 weeks (4 months) in advance — and explicitly flags Oct-Dec as "more popular times" that fill far ahead. NHS chapters, scout troops, youth groups, faith-community service teams targeting Thanksgiving/December service should email VolunteerWithUs@hopelink.org by mid-July at the latest. Group sizes are 5-15 (all members 16+). After September, expect 'no holiday-season availability' replies. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Hopelink Volunteer (Eastside / North & East King County)

items.label: Eastside Friends of Seniors — Drivers must be 21+; high-schoolers locked out of the most-needed role
items.detail: EFS's biggest unmet need is volunteer drivers (medical appointments, grocery, essential services), but the published age cutoff is 21+ for drivers — high schoolers are excluded from this track entirely. Non-driving roles open at 16. The under-promoted teen-friendly slot: 'Specialized Support' — web design, IT/tablet/phone troubleshooting for seniors, fundraising, admin tasks. STEM-track teens have a near-untapped pathway here that AOs read as both service AND skill-application. (verified 2026-04-27)

items.label: EFS — Minimum 6-month commitment + 2-5 hrs/month: this is relationship volunteering, not one-off shifts
items.detail: EFS requires a minimum of 2-5 hours/month for AT LEAST 6 months — designed to build a sustained relationship with one senior, not service-hour drop-ins. One-off-shift seekers chasing quick NHS hours will be turned away or redirected. Upside for college apps: same senior across 6+ months reads as authentic depth on Common App's activity description, vs. a transactional 'pulled some weeds once' line. Pitch this to families looking for ESSAY-quality service, not hour-quantity service. (verified 2026-04-27)

items.label: EFS — Companionship can be done OVER THE PHONE: a real path for non-driving teens & rural Eastside
items.detail: EFS lists companionship as in-person OR phone-based — which most parents miss because the page leads with transportation visuals. Phone companionship + remote IT/tech help means a 16-year-old without a license, a kid out in Snoqualmie Valley with no easy Bellevue/Redmond commute, or a teen with mobility limits can still build a 6-month relationship with a senior. Non-obvious workaround for the driver-21+ cliff. (verified 2026-04-27)

items.label: Hospital Junior Volunteer (multi-site) — application windows are tight + sometimes one-day-only
items.detail: For 2026: Orlando VA accepts ALL applications on a single day (Wed Apr 15, 2026); Holy Name Medical Center opens at exactly 7:00 a.m. on Tue May 5, 2026; Texas Health Alliance window is Jan 13–Mar 2; Houston Methodist West runs Feb 1–27. Parents who treat this as a 'when does summer start' search miss the slot. Calendar the open day, not the program start.

items.label: Hospital Junior Volunteer (multi-site) — acceptance is followed by a 2nd hurdle (TB test + drug screen + immunizations)
items.detail: Once selected, Texas Health, University Health (San Antonio), Houston Methodist, Atrium Health, UPMC Children's, and Medical City McKinney all require a criminal background check, urine drug screen, TB skin test (some require 2 PPD readings or a QuantiFERON Gold blood test), immunization review, sometimes a flu shot. Hospitals cover the cost but the lead-time can push the actual start date 2–3 weeks past the acceptance letter — front-load this before summer.

items.label: American Red Cross — Summer Youth Corps is a structured 11-week cohort, not drop-in volunteering
items.detail: Distinct from the generic 'become a volunteer' page: Summer Youth Corps requires 11 shifts across 11 weeks (one shift/week), age 13+, parent/guardian consent, and the volunteer Connection intake. Separately, a school-based Red Cross Club is a leadership/scholarship pathway — the school files a Club Constitution with the regional chapter and registers all members through Volunteer Connection. Two different commitments; they stack but aren't substitutes.

items.label: Special Olympics Unified Champion Schools — National Banner Recognition is a formal multi-year credential, not a participation badge
items.detail: Schools that sustain 10 standards (Unified Sports + Inclusive Youth Leadership + Whole School Engagement) across consecutive years earn National Banner Recognition Status. A student who launches/leads their HS's Unified Champion Schools effort earns a uniquely named credential AOs recognize — meaningfully stronger than 'volunteered at Special Olympics events.' Each year requires re-submitting a Commitment to Inclusion form via the state chapter (e.g., Special Olympics Washington).

items.label: Ronald McDonald House — meal-program is the only teen entry point, and it requires an adult chaperone
items.detail: Most individual volunteer roles are 18+ (Boston Harbor, Fort Worth chapters). The meal program opens at age 16 but requires a 1:2 adult-to-teen ratio at the Seattle chapter and a 21+ adult team leader at Charlotte; Southwest Virginia requires under-18s to be parent/guardian-accompanied in the kitchen. Practical implication for parents: a teen can't 'just sign up' — at least one adult has to commit alongside. Plan the cohort, not just the teen.

items.label: Crisis Text Line — strict 18+ + US SSN, but offers a unique grad-school practicum-credit pathway at 24 universities
items.detail: Hard 18+ requirement plus US Social Security Number (for background check) excludes high schoolers entirely — for under-18 mental-health crisis volunteering, look at TeenLine, Trevor Project youth ambassadors, or local TeenLink instead. For college-bound students pursuing social work, the Student Learning Practicum partners with 24 grad schools (Columbia SSW, NYU Silver, Rutgers SSW, Loyola Chicago, Hawaii Pacific, U Denver psychology, etc.) — practicum hours count toward the MSW 200–600-hour graduation requirement, completed remotely. Worth flagging to a senior choosing schools.
